rows.en:
Because on the day Ishikawa and Mr. Miyama eloped, blood came dripping from her ring.
Just like tears.
The one holding the ruby ring at the time was Mr. Miyama.
He'd left the ring in his suit pocket, so the lining got soaked with blood.
It caused a huge uproar.
And here's the awful part.
The teacher who'd been hitting on Ishikawa so hard suddenly shoved her away when she came close to look at the bloody suit.
He got scared, I guess.
And he seemed to think it was creepy.
So that very same day, he left her.{p}

So the elopement was over in a single day.
The ring was given back to her.{p}

And from the next day on, Ishikawa and Mr. Miyama started coming to school again.
They insisted it was pure coincidence they'd both vanished at the same time.
Once the two of them split up, the tears of blood flowing from the ring stopped.
And after that whole incident, she smiled even less than before.{p}

"No matter what happens from now on, my feelings won't change..."
She remembered the last words Ogura had said.
No matter what happens from now on...
Sweet words, right?
What do you think of that kind of thing?
Mr. Miyama had a change of heart over nothing more than the ring.
And she'd tried to go off with Mr. Miyama to forget the grief of losing the boy she loved.
But Ogura...
"No matter what happens from now on, my feelings won't change..."
That's what he'd said.
That's the kind of person he was.
All he did was make the ring shed tears of blood.
He didn't do anything else.
He didn't do anything wrong at all.
So she thought maybe it was a good thing this had shown her what Mr. Miyama was really like.{p}

And she put the ruby ring back on.
And then...
Hey, {c}{f:|}.
Don't you want to be close to the person you love?
No matter how close you are, you always want more and more, right?
Some people might not feel that way, I guess...
But her dead boyfriend seems to have been that type.
Do you know why I'm telling you this?{p}

...The ring wouldn't come off.
Off Ishikawa's finger.
At first, she didn't even notice.
I mean, it never occurred to her to take the ring off.{p}

Of course she wore it at home, and when she went to school, she wrapped a bandage around her ring finger to hide it.
Some teachers suspected there was a ring under that bandage.{p}

But whenever they pressed her about it, blood would come out of the ring.
Red blood would seep through the bandage.
Any teacher who saw that had no choice but to back off.
Even if she really was wearing a ring...{p}

After that, she spent her days without really feeling like finding a new boyfriend.
But one day, another guy came along and made a move on her.
He tried to persuade her that she shouldn't spend forever thinking only about someone who was gone.
He seems to have been a steady, decent guy.{p}

Scary, right?
But she wasn't scared at all.
That's when she became sure of it.
Of his strong feelings.
Of how deeply she was loved.
She vividly remembered him as he lay dying.{p}

His hand back then.
The hand that tried to grip hers with all its strength...
So she made up her mind.
She would live her whole life thinking of him.
And at that very moment...{p}

The red of the ruby ring changed to a clear white.
It turned transparent.
...Do you know what a white sapphire is?
It's a stone that's clear like a diamond, and it's the same mineral as ruby.
With that mineral, the red ones are called rubies, and the blue, white or pink ones are called sapphires.
That's right, her ruby turned into a white sapphire.
And the tears flowing from it changed from red to clear, too.
They turned into transparent tears, as if to show how pure his feelings were.
At the same time, the ring came loose...{p}

It slipped right off her finger.
It fit her fine, but it slid off as if someone had pulled it off, and fell to the floor...
Someone who didn't know the story might think the curse had been lifted.
But it's not about curses or anything.
She'd decided to live with her feelings for him, so the ring didn't need to bind her anymore.
He was so happy about how she felt.
That's why he shed clear tears, pure tears.{p}

...But I wonder how long that'll last.
You can probably tell from the story, but with her personality, I can't imagine her living the rest of her life without leaning on any man.
If someone's kind to her again...
If she changes her mind about living her whole life thinking of him...
He's so single-minded, after all.
Who knows what might happen, don't you think?
He trusted her feelings and released the ring's hold on her.{p}

If she betrays that trust...
Really, anything could happen.
"No matter what happens from now on, my feelings won't change..."
Those are sweet words.
But at the same time, they're scary words too, right?
His feelings really didn't change.
And from now on, forever...{p}

{c}{f:|}.
When you find someone you really love, why not {f:try giving them a ruby ring|try binding them with something}?
If your feelings are as strong as his, {f:you might manage a binding of bloody tears|you just might manage it}.
Hee hee...
Okay, let's hear the next story.
Oh right, if you want to hear that thirteen steps story I mentioned earlier, go take a look at the old school building first.
Okay?
So who's going to tell the next story?{p}

On the contrary, he was busy trying to win her over.
The more she treasured the ring, the more the teacher's ugly jealousy swelled.
Every night, Mr. Miyama would glare hatefully at the ruby ring and grumble under his breath, as if he were putting a curse on it.
Most of those words were aimed at Ishikawa's boyfriend, whom he'd never even seen.
But you know, a grudge against someone you've never met doesn't last that long.
Without Mr. Miyama himself even noticing, the target of that grudge shifted to Ishikawa.
I love her this much, and that woman won't even try to understand.
Rejecting my love is absolutely unforgivable.
...Would a normal person think like that?
Mr. Miyama must have been a seriously obsessive type.
And Ishikawa, who kept going to see him every day without giving up, was pretty tenacious too, I guess...{p}

And so the two of them went on, day after day, neither giving an inch.
The first one to break down was Ishikawa.{p}

She was a bit fragile emotionally, after all.
Until then, she'd had her boyfriend Ogura to support her, but now he was gone.
On top of that, she didn't even have the ring, practically the only keepsake she had of him.
She kept all that worry bottled up, and she fell ill.{p}

Then it was Mr. Miyama's turn to get uneasy.
Ishikawa, who'd been coming to see him practically every day, suddenly stopped coming.
She wasn't coming to school, either...
Did that mean she'd gotten sick or something?{p}
And at that moment, Mr. Miyama... was thinking something like this.{p}{c}{f:, which would it be for you|, what would you think if you were the teacher}?
Poor thing. I'll give her the ring back.
It's what she deserves for rejecting my love.

{f:What a nasty person|Hey}!
Do you seriously think that?
{f:You're just like Mr. Miyama|That's exactly what Mr. Miyama thought}.
{f:So you're actually pretty nasty, huh|That's kind of gross}.
{f:It was the same with Mr. Miyama, and apparently|Apparently Mr. Miyama}{f: he|} spat it out in disgust{f:| like this}.
"The fool.
It's what she deserves for rejecting my love again and again."
When love turns to hate, it hates a hundred times harder. That's exactly what this was.
To him, Ishikawa and the ruby ring were nothing but objects of hatred.
So with Ishikawa falling ill, he felt a little better.{p}

So, as one last act of spite against Ishikawa, he decided to throw the ring away.
It was an expensive piece, so he thought about selling it too, but apparently even he couldn't go that far.
If you ask me, once you've gone this far, there's not much difference between the two.
It was after school, at dusk, the hour when demons come out.
Mr. Miyama headed to the nearby river with that ring.{p}

There was no one around, but there seemed to be an awful lot of crows that day.
They say the black silhouettes of the crows against the red sunset were eerily beautiful.
Standing on the bridge, the teacher took the ruby ring out of his suit pocket.
The red ring caught the setting sun and gave off a strange, ominous glow.{p}

At that instant!
A flock of crows swooped down at the ring's glint.{p}

Damn it, crows love shiny things!
On reflex, the teacher threw the ring away.
But the crows didn't even glance at the ring. They attacked only the teacher.
A crow's beak is a sharp weapon, you know.
If a huge flock attacks you, a human gets eaten alive in no time.{p}

And sure enough, Mr. Miyama was found dead, his body horribly devoured.
There was almost nothing left but bones, so identifying him was really hard.
Apparently they figured it out from scraps of his clothes and stuff.
And some time after that, the ruby ring came back to Ishikawa.{p}

In the red, red sunset, Ogura comes walking toward her from far away.
And handing Ishikawa the ruby ring, he smiled and said,
"My feelings won't change."
And then he fades away, just like that.{p}

That was the dream she was having.
When she woke up and realized it was only a dream, she felt sad all over again.{p}

But just then, she heard a tap-tap, like someone knocking on her bedroom window.
Wondering what it was, she opened the curtain a little and...{p}

After that, Ishikawa recovered completely, and they say she's living a happy, healthy life.
...Only, you know, a lot of people around her die.
Men who pester her, mean upperclassmen... they've died in all kinds of accidents.
And every time someone dies, the ring glows redder and more eerily, they say.
These days the ring glows so much that Ishikawa supposedly wears a glove on her left hand only.
A blood-stained ring.
I don't know how many more years she'll live, but Ogura's heart stays by her side, along with the ring.
She'll live her whole life protected by the ring, without ever marrying.
Thinking only of the boy who died...{p}

Hey, {c}{f:|}.
If you died and left your sweetheart behind, what would you do?
Would you want to stay by their side, like Ogura?{p}Or would you let them be free, since the rest is their own life?
I'd want to stay by their side.
I'd let them be free.

I see, so being forgotten would be lonely after all.
Then you'll keep protecting them, just like Ogura, right?
No thanks, not for me.
Well, everyone's free to think what they want.{p}

Hee hee hee, that's right.
When you find someone you really love, you'd better give them something.
It doesn't have to be a ring.
And then you say,
"{f:My|My} feelings won't change."
Just like that.
Hee hee hee, good luck.
Okay, let's go on to the next story.
The thirteen steps story will have to wait for another time.
...So, who's next?{p}

Don't say such violent things.
Forget it. {c}{f:|}, just be quiet and listen.
She didn't give up on the ring.
After that, she went to Mr. Miyama every day and kept begging him to give the ring back.
But... one day, the two of them went missing.{p}

Really?
{c}{f:|}, you look like kind of a scaredy-cat to me.
Were you with someone, maybe?
Like a sweetheart...{p}

Ahahaha, judging by that face, I hit the nail on the head.
You don't have to hide it.
So that's why it was fun.
Yeah, nobody goes there, so it's probably a good place when you want to be alone together.
But you know, you really shouldn't go to the old school building too often.
...Not that I'm one to talk.{p}

Hey, {c}{f:|}.
Didn't anything weird happen back then?
If you're saying it was fun, either nothing happened at all, or you just didn't notice a thing.
When we went, something weird happened.{p}

The old school building is officially off-limits, right?
So we snuck inside, making sure no teachers spotted us.{p}

Then we went to that staircase and hung the tear-off calendar firmly on the stairwell wall.
It caught on the wall just right.{p}

"Now we're all set!"
Of the three of us, Yoko was having the most fun.{p}

"Yeah, now something's bound to happen."
Sanae was... pretty much the same as always, I think.
Same as ever, going at her own pace, I guess you'd say.
Her timing's kind of off.
So out of nowhere, she just started climbing the stairs.{p}

"One, two, three..."
Counting out loud in a big voice, like that.{p}
Yoko and I climbed the stairs, counting along just in case.{p}
"Ten... eleven... twelve... thirteen..................fourteen."{p}

It was fourteen steps, same as when Sanae counted.
I was a little disappointed, but we hadn't reached the second floor yet.
This was only the landing, so there was still half left.
I pulled myself together, and just as I was about to keep climbing...{p}
"Oh, wait a sec."{p}

Yoko was looking in the mirror on the landing, checking whether her hair was messed up.
Why now of all times, right?
And then Yoko, with a prim little face, goes,
"A girl has to look her best."
That's what she said.
She was in such a good mood, you'd never believe she'd been mad about the scary mood getting ruined just a minute before.
Yoko's a bit moody, I guess?{p}
"Okay, let's go up."{p}

With that, Yoko started climbing the stairs.
Of course, Sanae and I went up with her.{p}
